episode.title: Cariboo Signals - Arts, Culture & Digital Storytelling
episode.description:
Riley and Casey explore technology and society in rural communities. Today's focus: Arts, Culture & Digital Storytelling.

NEWS ROUNDUP: We break down [NPR Health News] It's been a record summer for foodborne illness and Penticton on edge as Bald Range evacuation alerts reach city boundary : My Cariboo Now, and explore what these developments mean for communities like ours.

RURAL CONNECTIONS: How can rural communities sustain trustworthy local storytelling when publishing barriers have collapsed but editorial accountability structures have disappeared? Topics include: Editorial gatekeeping vs. democratized publishing in rural media ecosystems, Accountability structures in legacy journalism vs. independent digital platforms, Discovery and indexing problems for locally-produced podcasts, newsletters, and self-published books, Beat reporting and institutional memory as irreplaceable journalistic functions, Sustained governance and staffing as the real barrier to local storytelling infrastructure.

Hosts: Riley (Tech optimist with an engineering background) and Casey (Community-first skeptic of tech promises).

COMMUNITY SPOTLIGHT: Central Cariboo Arts & Culture Society

discussion.central_question: How can rural communities sustain trustworthy local storytelling when publishing barriers have collapsed but editorial accountability structures have disappeared?
discussion.riley_position: Digital tools have democratized publishing and created genuine opportunities for independent creators to reach audiences legacy outlets cannot; the format itself doesn't prevent accountability—it requires deliberate choice from individual creators.
riley_key_evidence: Podcasting eliminates printing costs, delivery trucks, and ad-sales overhead that traditional outlets require
First Nations and governments can now publish primary statements directly, bypassing traditional media framing
Some independent journalists have built explicit correction policies and transparency into newsletters and podcasts through deliberate effort
discussion.casey_position: Tools alone don't create editorial discipline; institutional accountability structures (editor accountability, corrections columns, legal review, job consequences) historically enforced trustworthiness in ways individual creators rarely replicate without external pressure.
casey_key_evidence: Newsroom staffing at regional papers has been shrinking for over a decade, leaving gaps filled by unedited social posts
A newspaper's credibility came from a chain of accountability—editors who could be fired, corrections in the same physical paper, lawyers on retainer
Beat reporting requires sustained institutional memory across multiple meetings months apart, which single podcast episodes reacting to press releases cannot provide
discussion.resolution: They agreed that the core problem is not technological but structural: someone must be paid or formally assigned to do sustained curation and maintenance work. They pivoted toward a shared solution—a regional index of local storytelling that would require one part-time position to maintain, and asked listeners whether such infrastructure should exist and who would maintain it.
